title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 323
paragraphs: Then Sesostris, having returned to Egypt and having taken vengeance on his brother, employed the multitude that he had brought in from the peoples whose lands he had subdued as follows. These were the men who drew the stones — of very great size — that in the reign of this king were brought to the temple of Hephaestus; and these were also compelled to dig all the channels that now exist in Egypt. Thus, with no such purpose in mind, they caused Egypt, which before was all fit for riding and driving, to be no longer so from that time onwards; for from then on Egypt, though it is plain country, has become entirely unfit for riding and driving, and the cause has been these channels, which are many and run in every direction. The reason the king cut up the land thus was this: those of the Egyptians whose cities were not on the river but in the middle of the country, being in want of water when the river had gone down from them, found their drink brackish because they had it from wells.
